newsitem.title: USA: Cortex drug shown to improve memory, stock soars.
newsitem.headline: Cortex drug shown to improve memory, stock soars.

text.p: Cortex Pharmaceuticals Inc. said Monday a drug it is developing to treat Alzheimer's disease and schizophrenia has been found to improve memory in rats, sparking a surge in its stock.
The stock of the Irvine, Calif.-based company soared $1.9375, or more than 67 percent, to $4.8125 on the Nasdaq market at mid-afternoon.
The drug, Ampalex, is the lead compound from a new class of chemical compounds, known as Ampakines, that enhance the functioning of brain neurons that are active in memory performance.
Results of the study, conducted by Dr. Sam Deadwyler at Wake Forest University, were presented at the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience in Washington.
In the study, Ampalex was administered to rats, who demonstated improved performance on memory tasks.
"This study marks a significant advance in our understanding of how Ampakines work," Dr. Vincent Simmon, Cortex president and chief executive, said in a statement.

"We have known for some time that these drugs enhance the functioning of AMPA receptors over the short time frames that are associated with firing of neurons. It now apears that these short-term effects lead to much longer-term changes in neuronal activity that are reflected in the behaviour of the animal."
